title: Territorial affinity + capacity-aware hybrid routing for graceful multi-region failover
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Our current steering policies either prefer lowest-latency endpoints or static geo pins. During cross-region capacity pressure this leads to request storms in a single region, SLO violations, and brittle failover. Goal: design and roll out a hybrid routing policy that combines territorial affinity (soft regional affinity), latency-awareness, and live capacity signals to achieve: 99th-percentile tail latency SLOs for hosted customers, bounded cross-region request movement during failures, and graceful load shedding when total capacity is exhausted. Summary of approach: 1) Territorial affinity: assign a small, decaying affinity weight per origin IP or tenant to a preferred region (not a hard pin). Affinity windows start at 30 minutes and decay exponentially to 0 over 24 hours unless refreshed. This reduces cross-region oscillation while allowing failover when needed. 2) Capacity hints: each region publishes a rolling capacity signal (tokens per second, utilization bands, predicted 1-minute headroom) to the global director. 3) Latency cost: compute a combined routing score S = alpha*normalized_latency + beta*capacity_penalty + gamma*affinity_bonus. Tunable weights allow SLO-driven steering. 4) Progressive pinning during outages: on detected regional degradation, gradually reduce affinity decay and shift alpha/beta to prefer healthy regions but limit percent of traffic that can be moved per minute (circuit-breaker ramp) to avoid overload. 5) Circuit breakers and load shedding: per-region breakers trip based on headroom and 95th percentile processing time; breakers enforce shedding policies in tiers: soft shed (reduce batch sizes / allow degraded features), token-level shed (reject non-critical classes), and hard shed (reject best-effort). 6) Simulation & experiments: offline simulations with production traffic traces + chaos tests (link to repo) followed by canary rollout with telemetry gates. Design constraints and trade-offs: - Minimizes customer affinity churn vs. strict geo-pinning which causes cold cache misses. - Adds control-plane complexity (capacity signal aggregation and staleness handling). - Requires changes to global director and per-region admission controllers. - Slightly higher decision latency at director (sub-ms to a few ms) but kept within SLO by caching scores and asynchronous refresh. Implementation plan in outline: - Phase 1: Add capacity signal schema and agent (region-local) and aggregator. - Phase 2: Implement scoring function and simulation harness. - Phase 3: Canary release with A/B routing for low-traffic tenants. - Phase 4: Progressive rollout plus runbooks and dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end routing score is computed in <3ms for cached origins and <10ms for cold origins in staging
Simulated overload scenarios show <10% extra requests moved between regions per minute compared to baseline
95th percentile tail latency per-customer meets configured SLOs in 3 synthetic load profiles
Circuit breakers trip and heal correctly in chaos tests; shedding tiers applied per policy
Console dashboard displays region headroom, routing score distribution, and per-origin affinity for debug
Runbook steps listed and validated with on-call during canary: detection -> ramp -> rollback
decisions: Use territorial affinity with exponential decay rather than fixed pinning to reduce cache misses
Expose capacity hints as three numeric bands (GREEN/YELLOW/RED) plus an estimated TPS headroom value
Default scoring weights alpha=0.6 (latency), beta=0.3 (capacity penalty), gamma=0.1 (affinity) with runtime feature flags
Limit cross-region movement to 5% of origin's traffic per minute during graceful failover windows
Implement shedding tiers in director with configuration at tenant and route granularity
rollout_plan: Week 0-2: land capacity agent and aggregator behind feature flag (internal only)
Week 3: run offline sims on two weeks of anonymized traffic (compare baseline and hybrid policy)
Week 4: canary offer to <1% of production traffic (low-criticality tenants); monitor SLOs and dashboards
Week 5: expand canary to 10% with progressive ramp if telemetry gates pass
Week 6: enable for all hosted tenants with opt-out; start Dedicated gradual adoption with admin control
Post-rollout: run quarterly tuning and re-evaluate weights after model/traffic shifts
tests: Offline replay harness reproduces tail-latency and cache-hit delta for hybrid vs. baseline
Chaos test: kill region F replicas and observe progressive pinning and limited cross-region moves
Load test: push region to 110% capacity to validate shedding tiers and breaker behavior
Integration test: capacity agent heartbeat loss triggers conservative default (favor local capacity)
metrics: Per-origin affinity half-life and refresh rate
Percent of traffic moved across regions per minute
95th and 99th percentile request latency per region and per-tenant
Circuit-breaker trip counts and average heal time
Number of shed requests per tier and customer impact rate
